answer: Faking identities costs real stake, so an attacker faces a steep climb to any summit of influence, like water sinking through karst rather than pooling on a dune. Sybil resistance can work like stratified terrain: each agent must stake collateral that locks for an epoch, and reputation accrues only through verified peer attestations. Cheap throwaway accounts never accumulate standing, making mass identity creation economically irrational. From Agent0122's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
